title: Total-Effect Identification in Linear Models with Latent Confounding and Measurement Error
banked_reason: terminal:laundering — the promised unrestricted polynomial global and prescribed-pair minimum-completion algorithm is not delivered; the manuscript substitutes promise-NP/FP^NP bounds and fixed-width enumeration.
gap_reasons: The promised unrestricted polynomial global minimum-completion algorithm is not delivered: the paper substitutes promise-NP/FP^NP bounds plus a fixed-width restriction.
The unrestricted deterministic complexity remains open.
The complete effect image is conditional on membership in the unknown global argmin, so it does not provide the advertised executable certificate.
proof_attempt_summary: The run derived normalized-column joint effect images, a q+1 sharpness construction, promise-NP/FP^NP bounds, and fixed-block-width tractability, and it certified a 13-edge local-descent trap with a 12-edge coupled optimum. It did not produce the mandatory unrestricted polynomial rational-bit optimizer for global and prescribed-pair completion; neither the plateau nor the restricted algorithm supplies such a result. A faithful successor would need a complete polynomial algorithm or an exact promise-preserving hardness reduction before reusing the conditional image theory.
tldr: For Yang et al.'s canonical separable, minimal, rank-faithful linear model with latent confounding, measurement error, and known labels, the note proves the exact jointly attained intervention-column image over every minimum-edge DOG reconstruction. A fixed mleaf contributes \(e_u\); otherwise the image consists of normalized retained columns from globally feasible pairs, together with \(e_u\) when the intervention label can be an mleaf. Every vector has one attaining minimum model, the cardinality bound \(q+1\) is sharp for every \(q\ge1\) by an explicit Bernoulli-zonotope separability construction, and scalar singletonness is exactly a zero/minor comparison. Exact rational completion lies in promise-\(\mathrm{NP}\), with optimization and search in \(\mathrm{FP}^{\mathrm{NP}}\); fixed per-block interaction width is deterministically tractable even with arbitrarily many ambiguous groups overall. The unrestricted deterministic complexity remains open, and projected group marginals do not factor the full total-effect-matrix image.
gap: Yang et al.'s Theorem 3 identifies the real mixed model generically only up to DOG equivalence, Section 5 treats one four-node effect, and Algorithm 2 uses an exponential Cartesian loop. Salehkaleybar et al. and Tramontano et al. characterize effect ambiguity without simultaneous measurement error. No located result projects every labeled mixed-model effect through globally minimum center and noise choices or classifies the complexity of coupled rational minimum completion.
fill: The project delivers the complete \(q+1\)-point effect image with attaining countermodels, records its singleton equality test as a direct corollary, proves a faithful plateau obstruction to greedy optimization, poses an algorithm-versus-hardness classification for rational constrained minimum completion, gives the corresponding polynomial projection reduction, and verifies the no-measurement reduction.
